To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the diet modulates cecal bacterial diversity and physiological traits across the BXD genetic reference population.

the high-fat diet (60% fat) induces a shift in the cecum bacterial microbiota and a substantial increase in the cecal sIga level in BXD mice, and that the host genetics modulates the bacterial composition at the phylum and genus levels in chow diet.

(1) the cecal microbiome of the BXD family is modulated by both host genetics and diet; (2) the cecal sIgs of the BXD mice are modulated by both diet and host genetics; and (3) the liver metabolome of the BXDs is modulated by diet and host genetics.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of genetic variation on the cecum bacterial communities and their relation to host phenotypes in a mouse model.
the genetic basis of phenotypic diversity and how it is modulated by environmental influences.
the genetic basis of the response of mice to different levels of dietary fat, and the role of the cecal microbiome in this response.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the genetic background and the environmental factors (dietary and otherwise) are the two major determinants of phenotypic variability.
the HFD induces substantial changes in the composition and diversity of the cecal microbiota, with the greatest impact in the D2B6F2 cohort.
diet has an important effect on the cecum microbial composition, but the impact of host genetics is still significant.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
diet modulates cecal bacterial diversity, physiological phenotypes and host genetics.
we have identified a number of genetic loci that influence the cecum microbial community, and we have also shown that diet can have a profound effect in altering the composition of the cecums.
the BXD family of mice is a useful genetic model to study the impact of host genetics on the cecum bacterial community and the impact of HFD on the host immune system and metabolism.
The main takeaway from our work is that
diet is a critical environmental factor that can modulate phenotypic traits in a manner that is dependent on the genetic background of the host.
the cecum bacterial community composition can be modulated by both genetic and environmental factors, which in turn affects the host phenotype.
the cecum bacterial community is highly responsive to dietary manipulation and that this community is highly responsive and modulated by the genetics of the host.
